title: Microheuristic stitching — thoughtlog
content:
Goal / mental model:
This is a personal scratchpad for assembling a set of small, composable heuristics (micro-heuristics) that we can "stitch" together to handle messy tokenization/label boundaries we keep hitting in user annotation. Not a final spec — more of an operational cookbook + triage log so I can test quickly and hand off clearer rules to the team later.

Why micro-heuristics?
- Many long, brittle rules fail at the margin (e.g., multiword brand names, punctuation adjacency).
- Small orthogonal checks applied in order (confidence, punctuation, length ratio, canonicalization) are performant and easier to audit.
- Want deterministic, idempotent pipeline behavior (reproducible fixes, minimal annotation churn).

Common failure patterns I've seen this week (examples from sample batch B-17):
1) Split tokens across punctuation that should be a single label
   - "ACME-Connect Pro" annotated as [ACME-Connect] + [Pro] by annotators -> should be single product entity.
2) URL-like tokens split into id + path segments annotated inconsistently
   - "example.com/login?id=123" sometimes labeled as domain only, sometimes domain+path.
3) IDs appended to names via slash or hash treated as distinct entities
   - "Invoice/3344" vs "Invoice".
4) Case-only variants annotated as separate types (e.g., 'iPhone' vs 'iphone')

Micro-heuristics (draft list, order matters):
A. canonicalize-and-check: normalize whitespace, collapse repeated punctuation, unicode NFKC; if canonicalization merges two labeled spans into continuous characters, mark for merge candidate.
B. join-on-hyphen-rule: if two adjacent labels separated by a hyphen or slash and the combined char length < 60 and combined token count <= 4, prefer a single label unless explicit contextual delimiter (newline, sentence break).
C. url-prefix-policy: if the leftmost token matches domain-regex and there is an attached path/query, ask labeler to prefer full-url span for domain-sensitive labels; for generic 'org' labels only keep domain.
D. trailing-id-attachment: if trailing segment is purely numeric or short alphanumeric <=8 and prefixed by '/', '#', or ':', keep separate label only if context indicates an 'ID' type (invoice, ticket); otherwise attach to base entity.
E. case-preserve-check: preserve capitalization if it changes meaning (proper nouns) — fallback: prefer lowercase normalization only for tokens matching dictionary words.
F. short-span-abstain: if automated confidence (model or annotator agreement) < 0.5 and span < 3 chars, mark for manual review rather than auto-merge.

Decision examples (hand-checked):
- "ACME-Connect Pro": canonicalize => "acme-connect pro" -> join-on-hyphen-rule applies => merged label = "ACME-Connect Pro" (product). Rationale: product names often include hyphen + suffix.
- "example.com/login?id=123": url-prefix-policy suggests full-url for use-cases where domain alone is insufficient (support routing). For embeddings we might keep domain-only. Need downstream policy flag.
- "Invoice/3344": trailing-id-attachment sees numeric suffix => separate ID label if field type == 'invoice' in schema; otherwise attach.

Operational notes for pipeline implementers:
- Each micro-heuristic should be a small, testable function with a clear boolean outcome and reason code (e.g., JOINED_HYPHEN, SPLIT_ID_ATTACHED).
- Maintain an ordered list and expose an 'explain' string per change for audit logs (helpful for customer questions and for the Console trace views).
- Provide a 'noisy_toggle' to run heuristics in a non-destructive preview mode for 48h on live traffic to gather false-positive rates.

Quick metrics to collect during preview:
- percent_changed_by_heuristic (per-heuristic)
- manual_overturn_rate (human reviewers revert change)
- precision_estimate (sampled) and recall_estimate when gold exists
Goal: keep manual_overturn_rate < 6% for any heuristic; prioritize heuristics with high change volume for immediate tuning.

Open questions / things I need to test:
- How do heuristics interact with prefix/KV caching? If we change spans, cached embeddings may be invalid — need to annotate cache-busting metadata. (Ask Eng: SRE/Serving)
- Should we prefer attaching trailing IDs for internal customers (private deployments) where their schemas are known? Likely yes — need a policy flag per-deployment.
- Is there a simple regex set that covers >95% of URL/ID suffix cases? Start with: domain regex + [/#:]?
- Human readability: avoid merging spans that create longer than 80 chars entity — these are probably annotation noise.

Small experiment plan (next 2 weeks):
1) Implement join-on-hyphen and trailing-id-attachment in local transformer pass.
2) Run on B-17 batch (10k sentences) in preview mode; log changes and reason codes.
3) Sample 400 changed examples, do blind manual review (pair annotators) -> compute overturn rate.
4) If overturn <6% and changes reduce label variance by >22%, roll to wider preview.

Sample rows (format: ORIGINAL || CURRENT_LABELS || SUGGESTED_HEURISTIC && NOTES)
"ACME-Connect Pro" || [ACME-Connect], [Pro] || JOINED_HYPHEN && merge to single product label
"example.com/login?id=123" || [example.com], [login], [id=123] || URL_PREFIX && prefer full-url span for routing use-case
"Invoice/3344" || [Invoice], [3344] || TRAILING_ID && separate ID label only if schema==invoice
"iPhone 12" || [iphone], [12] || CASE_PRESERVE && preserve capitalized Product name
"Acme Inc." || [Acme], [Inc.] || JOINED_HYPHEN (well, join on adjacency) && company suffix attach

Notes to self: keep this doc small and pragmatic. Turn into a GH issue with code sketch and unit tests next. Add Harriet + Luis to review once I have the preview logs. Tag for discussion in #labeling during the 11/24 sync.

—— END SCRATCHPAD —
